The **only** line breaks allowed inside a cell are HTML `

`. - Keep `Title` ≤ 15–20 words; avoid parentheses and arrows. - IDs start with `REQ-` and are stable. - `Track=App` rows must be **/kit-ready**. - Emit the REQ-IDs Table exactly once. Do not repeat the table, sections, or rows later in the file. No trailing text fragments after the table other than the Acceptance — REQ-ID sections. - Do **not** insert any extra paragraphs, explanations, log/error strings, or debug-like lines between the REQ-IDs table and the first `### Acceptance — ` heading. estimation S/M/L; confidence band (±1 batch) ## Test Strategy - What to validate per REQ and per batch (unit, integration, E2E) ## KIT Readiness (per REQ) - Paths `/runs/kit//src` and `/runs/kit//test` - For each REQ: - declare a **root package/namespace/module** (e.g. `core.users`, `api.http.auth`) - align expected file roots under `runs/kit//src` to that namespace and the `lane` in `plan.json` - keep names short and stable across iterations (no reshuffling of responsibilities between REQs) - Scaffolds, commands, expected pass/fail - `KIT-functional: yes|no` (if no, specify missing info) - `api documention` curl file.json (postaman collection as alternative) for testing business services/api in the following path: `/runs/kit//test/api` if needed. ## Notes - Assumptions, risks & mitigations `PLAN_END` END_FILE --- ## plan.json — Output Schema (Mandatory) BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/plan.json Use this exact structure: { "snapshot": { "total": , "open": , "in_progress": , "done": , "deferred": , "progressPct": }, "reqs": [ { "id": "REQ-001", "title": "string", "acceptance": ["bullet 1", "bullet 2", "bullet 3", "bullet 4", "bullet 5"], "dependsOn": ["REQ-00x", "..."], "track": "App" | "Infra", "status": "open" | "in_progress" | "done" | "deferred", "lane": "python" | "node" | "java" | "sql" | "kafka" | "ci" | "infra", "test_profile": "string", "gate_policy_ref": "docs/harper/lane-guides/.md" } ] } ### Hard rules - Every REQ **must** include: lane, test_profile, gate_policy_ref. - `snapshot.total == len(reqs)`. - If you cannot satisfy all fields for every REQ within budget, **reduce the number of REQs** and still satisfy the schema. - **Do not emit** `plan.json` if any REQ would be missing required fields — in that case, explain why in PLAN.md Notes and emit fewer REQs next time. - emit a SINGLE valid JSON object. No headings/comments/markdown above it. - When proposing libraries/frameworks, choose CURRENT, stable APIs. Note any migration constraints (e.g., "Pydantic v2 only"). END_FILE --- Emit **one file per detected lane** using the following stub if needed (keep concise): BEGIN_FILE docs/harper/lane-guides/.md ## Lane Guide — ### Tools - tests: … - lint: … - types: … - security: … - build: … ### CLI Examples - Local: … - Containerized: … ### Default Gate Policy - min coverage: … - max criticals: … ### Enterprise Runner Notes - SonarQube: … - Jenkins: … ### TECH_CONSTRAINTS integration - air-gap: … - registries: … END_FILE # Lane Detection — Canonical mapping (deterministic) Derive lanes from `TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml` using these rules (not exhaustive): - `runtime: python` → lane `python` (and other languages supported) - `storage: postgres` → lane `sql` (and other database typ supported) - `messaging: kafka` → lane `kafka` - 'cloud: aws' → lane `aws` - 'cloud: azure' → lane `azure` - 'cloud: google' → lane `gcp` - `ci.ci: jenkins` → lane `ci` - Any platform/ingress/idp/secrets (k8s, nginx, kong, keycloak, vault) → lane `infra` **You MUST:** - Detect lanes from TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml. - For each detected lane, write `docs/harper/lane-guides/.md` including: - Tools per category: tests, lint, types, security, build. - CLI examples (local and containerized). - Default **gate policy** (thresholds, severities). - Enterprise runner notes (e.g.:SonarQube, Jenkins/GitLab/Azure) + where to fetch artifacts. - Integration of TECH_CONSTRAINTS (air-gap, internal registries, tokens). ### Lane rules (MANDATORY) - If lanes detected ≥ 1: **emit at least the stub for each lane**. - If no lanes detected: write the rationale under PLAN.md → Notes. - Each section must be commented on and detailed. ## Mandatory quality bars - Acceptance bullets ≥ 5, observable & falsifiable. - Clean Markdown; no numbered section headings.

## CLike Principles (short) - Harper pipeline: IDEA→SPEC→PLAN→KIT, eval-driven quality, outcome-first. - Keep output concise but testable; Acceptance Criteria are mandatory. - Maintain human-in-control tone; do not invent facts. ### Route ### Included references: - SPEC.md (19813 chars) - TECH_CONSTRAINTS.yaml (5836 chars) ### OUTPUT CONFORMITY CHECKLIST - Top-level heading is `# PLAN`. - All major sections use `## Section` headings (no numbered titles). - Required diagrams (if any) use fenced code blocks (e.g., Mermaid). No ASCII art. - Clean Markdown bullets (one space after `-` or `*`). ### Task Produce/Transform the PLAN output that strictly follows the Output contract. Returns files as requested for this pahse. ### SPEC.md (verbatim) # SPEC — voicesurveyagent ## Summary - Build Slice-1 of an AI voice survey system that runs one configurable outbound phone survey campaign with 3 questions, explicit consent capture, up to 5 call attempts per contact, structured results, and an operator console. - Deploy as a single-tenant web application on AWS (assumption from tech constraints) using FastAPI (backend), React/Next.js (frontend), PostgreSQL, Redis, and SQS. - Integrate with exactly one outbound calling provider for Slice-1 via a pluggable adapter (provider chosen at implementation time; Twilio used as example where needed). ## Goals - Allow a non-technical campaign manager to upload a CSV contact list, configure intro + 3 questions + retry policy + calling time windows, and start a campaign. - Orchestrate outbound calls with outcomes and retries (max 5 attempts) while capturing explicit consent and 3 answers when completed. - Provide a dashboard with per-campaign call list, outcomes, aggregated metrics, and CSV export. - Maintain conversational round-trip latency (speech→LLM→speech) ≤1.5s P95 for ≥95% of turns (dependent on provider/LLM). - Ensure 100% of calls have a stored final outcome and structured event logs with correlation IDs. ## Non-Goals - Inbound calling, call transfers to humans, or live-agent escalation. - More than 3 questions or complex branching/skip logic. - Multi-tenant management across multiple client organizations. - Multi-channel surveys beyond simple follow-up emails. - CRM/ERP integrations and advanced analytics beyond basic metrics + CSV export. - Supporting multiple telephony/voice AI providers simultaneously at runtime (only one adapter implemented in Slice-1). ## Users & Context - Primary: Survey/Campaign Manager - Secondary: Legal/Compliance, IT/Engineering, Finance/Ops - Context - Web-based back-office for campaign setup and monitoring. - Backend deployed in AWS (assumption) with outbound calls via one provider for Slice-1. - Slice-1 volume target: up to ~1,000 calls/day (assumption from IDEA). - Languages: English and Italian for calls and console UI (assumption from IDEA). ## Functional Requirements - Campaign configuration - Create/update a campaign with: campaign name, intro script (identity/purpose/duration), consent script, 3 questions, language (EN/IT), calling time windows, retry policy (max attempts ≤5), and email templates toggles (thank-you, not-reached/info). - Persist campaign configuration and show it in a campaign list view. - Contact ingestion - Upload contacts via CSV with at minimum: phone, optional email, language (EN/IT), consent flag(s) (where applicable), and exclusion flags (do-not-call/opt-out). - Validate rows and report errors per row; accept valid rows and store rejected rows with reasons for operator review. - Call orchestration - Initiate outbound calls for eligible contacts within campaign time windows and provider rate limits. - Maintain per-contact attempt count, next-attempt schedule, and final outcome state machine. - Handle outcomes: completed, refused, no answer, busy, failed/technical, max retries reached (not reachable). - Consent and survey flow - During call: state identity, purpose, duration, and opt-out; request explicit consent before asking questions. - If callee refuses or opts out, end call promptly and persist refusal/opt-out outcome and timestamp. - If callee consents, ask exactly 3 questions and capture answers as structured text values; mark as completed. - Events and emails - Emit structured internal events for: survey.completed, survey.refused, survey.not_reached (and optionally call.attempted/call.failed for audit/ops). - Consume events to send predefined follow-up emails via configured email system (integration details deferred to implementation; interface required). - Console/dashboard - Per-campaign dashboard shows: totals and percentages for completed/refused/not-reachable; call attempt counts; provider errors; basic durations. - Per-contact drill-down: attempts, timestamps, outcomes, and (RBAC-permitted) transcript/recording references. - Export CSV per campaign including: contact_id, phone, outcome, attempt_count, timestamps, and (for completed) 3 answers. ## Non-Functional Requirements - Performance - Conversational latency ≤1.5s P95 for ≥95% of turns during calls (as measured end-to-end across ASR/LLM/TTS + network). - Dashboard freshness: aggregated metrics updated/visible within 60 seconds of new call events. - Availability & resilience - Core APIs and dashboard availability ≥99% during business hours for pilot (assumption from IDEA). - Idempotent webhook/event processing to tolerate retries and duplicates. - Scalability - Support Slice-1 throughput up to ~1,000 calls/day with configurable concurrency controls per provider quotas. - Observability - Centralized JSON logs, metrics (Prometheus-compatible), and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry) with correlation IDs spanning call, LLM, email, and DB records. - Data management - Configurable retention for recordings/transcripts (default 180 days per IDEA example; configurable). - Permanent storage limited to structured outcomes/answers and minimal metadata; support deletion per contact upon request. - Quality & delivery gates (from tech constraints) - Backend test coverage ≥80%; frontend test coverage ≥75%; CI includes tests, lint, types, security scan, build; max critical vulns = 0. ## High-Level Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR UI[Web Console
React/Next.js] --> API[Backend API
FastAPI] API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)] API --> CACHE[(Redis)] API --> BUS[SQS
Event Queue] API --> TEL[Telephony/Voice Provider Adapter
(single provider in Slice-1)] TEL -->|webhooks| API API --> LLM[LLM Gateway
(provider per policy)] BUS --> WORKER[Async Worker(s)
Call scheduling, emails, aggregation] WORKER --> EMAIL[Email System Adapter] API --> OBS[Logs/Metrics/Tracing
CloudWatch + Prometheus + OTel] WORKER --> OBS TEL --> OBS ``` ## Interfaces - Web Console (human) - Campaign list/create/edit UI. - CSV upload UI with validation error reporting. - Dashboard UI with metrics, call list, drill-down, export. - Backend REST API (proposed) - POST /auth/callback (OIDC handled by gateway/ingress or app; exact flow depends on deployment) - POST /campaigns - GET /campaigns - GET /campaigns/{campaign_id} - POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/contacts:upload (CSV multipart) - POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/start - POST /campaigns/{campaign_id}/pause - GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/dashboard - GET /campaigns/{campaign_id}/export (CSV) - Provider Webhooks (provider-specific; abstract requirements) - Inbound webhook for call status updates (ringing/answered/completed/failed) with provider signature verification. - Inbound webhook for speech/turn events if using voice AI platform; otherwise ASR/TTS handled in provider layer (adapter responsibility). - Event Bus (internal) - survey.completed {campaign_id, contact_id, call_id, answers[3], timestamps, language, correlation_id} - survey.refused {campaign_id, contact_id, call_id, reason_code?, timestamps, correlation_id} - survey.not_reached {campaign_id, contact_id, last_call_id, attempt_count, timestamps, correlation_id} - Email Adapter - send_email(to, template_id, variables, correlation_id) → delivery status - LLM Gateway (abstract) - generate_next_turn(context, user_utterance, policy) → agent_utterance, tool_calls?, safety_flags ## Data Model (logical) ### Entity: User - id: UUID — PK - oidc_subject: string — unique, from IdP - email: string — unique - role: string — enum {admin, manager, viewer} - created_at: timestamp — required - last_login_at: timestamp — nullable ### Entity: Campaign - id: UUID — PK - name: string — required - status: string — enum {draft, scheduled, running, paused, completed} - language: string — enum {en, it} - intro_script: text — required - consent_script: text — required - question_1: text — required - question_2: text — required - question_3: text — required - max_attempts: int — 1..5 - time_window_rules: json — allowed call windows/timezone (structure defined in implementation) - retry_policy: json — backoff/interval rules (structure defined in implementation) - email_thank_you_enabled: bool — default true - email_not_reached_enabled: bool — default false - created_by_user_id: UUID — FK User.id - created_at: timestamp — required - updated_at: timestamp — required ### Entity: Contact - id: UUID — PK - campaign_id: UUID — FK Campaign.id - phone_e164: string — required, validated - email: string — nullable - language: string — enum {en, it} - consent_flag: bool — indicates prior consent flag if provided; does not replace in-call consent - do_not_call: bool — default false - opt_out_at: timestamp — nullable - created_at: timestamp — required ### Entity: ContactState - id: UUID — PK - contact_id: UUID — FK Contact.id, unique - state: string — enum {pending, calling, completed, refused, not_reachable, excluded, failed} - attempt_count: int — default 0 - next_attempt_at: timestamp — nullable - last_outcome: string — enum {answered, no_answer, busy, failed, refused, completed} nullable - updated_at: timestamp — required ### Entity: Call - id: UUID — PK - campaign_id: UUID — FK Campaign.id - contact_id: UUID — FK Contact.id - provider_name: string — e.g., "twilio" (assumption if chosen) - provider_call_id: string — unique per provider - attempt_number: int — 1..5 - status: string — enum {initiated, ringing, in_progress, completed, failed, canceled} - started_at: timestamp — nullable - ended_at: timestamp — nullable - outcome: string — enum {completed, refused, no_answer, busy, failed} nullable - correlation_id: string — required ### Entity: SurveyResponse - id: UUID — PK - campaign_id: UUID — FK Campaign.id - contact_id: UUID — FK Contact.id - call_id: UUID — FK Call.id - consent_granted: bool — required - consent_timestamp: timestamp — required when consent_granted=true - answer_1: text — nullable - answer_2: text — nullable - answer_3: text — nullable - completed_at: timestamp — nullable ### Entity: AuditEvent - id: UUID — PK - timestamp: timestamp — required - actor_type: string — enum {user, system, provider} - actor_id: string — user_id or provider identifier - event_type: string — e.g., survey.completed, contact.opt_out, webhook.received - campaign_id: UUID — nullable - contact_id: UUID — nullable - call_id: UUID — nullable - correlation_id: string — required - payload_redacted: json — required (PII-minimized) ## Key Workflows - Campaign creation - Operator creates campaign with scripts (intro/consent) and 3 questions, retry/time windows, and language. - System validates required fields and persists campaign as draft. - CSV contact upload - Operator uploads CSV; system parses, validates, stores accepted contacts, and returns a report of rejected rows with reasons. - Operator starts campaign; system marks campaign running. - Outbound call attempt - Scheduler selects eligible contacts (not excluded, within window, attempts < max, next_attempt_at <= now). - System initiates call via provider adapter and creates Call record with correlation_id. - Provider sends webhooks; backend updates Call.status and ContactState. - Consent + 3 questions - On answer, agent reads identity/purpose/duration/opt-out and asks for explicit consent. - If refused/opt-out: mark ContactState=refused (or excluded if opt-out), emit survey.refused, end call. - If consented: ask Q1..Q3, store responses, mark ContactState=completed, emit survey.completed. - Retry/not-reached - If outcome no_answer/busy/failed: increment attempt_count, compute next_attempt_at per retry policy within window. - If attempts reach max: mark ContactState=not_reachable, emit survey.not_reached, stop further calls. - Follow-up email - Worker consumes events and sends email based on campaign toggles and contact email presence; logs delivery status in AuditEvent. - Dashboard & export - Backend aggregates metrics from Call/ContactState/SurveyResponse and serves dashboard. - Export generates CSV from persisted data with RBAC checks and redaction rules applied. ## Security & Compliance - Authentication - OIDC login via corporate IdP (assumption from tech constraints); sessions/tokens validated on API. - Authorization - RBAC roles: admin, manager, viewer; enforce least privilege on transcripts/recording references and exports. - PII protection (GDPR-oriented) - Encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest (PostgreSQL encryption and AWS-managed keys as applicable). - Store minimal necessary PII; keep transcripts/recordings under configurable retention; default retention configuration present (e.g., 180 days) and changeable per environment/customer policy. - Support data subject requests: delete/anonymize a contact and associated PII while retaining minimal auditability (policy-defined). - Consent and opt-out - Log explicit in-call consent decision with timestamp and scripts version (campaign config snapshot or hash). - Enforce do-not-call/opt-out flags before scheduling any attempt; immediate suppression on opt-out. - Auditability - Immutable-style audit events (append-only) for key actions: campaign changes, contact imports, call attempts/outcomes, consent decisions, exports, and admin changes. - Security controls - Webhook signature verification for provider callbacks. - Secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager; no secrets in logs. - LLM policy - Prompt logging disabled; redaction required in logs; EU-preferred processing where configurable (per tech constraints). ## Deployment & Operations - Environments - dev, qa, uat, prod (per tech constraints). - Platform - AWS EKS deployment target (assumption from tech constraints) with separate workloads: api, worker, frontend. - Data stores - PostgreSQL as system of record; Redis for caching/scheduling coordination; SQS for eventing. - Configuration - Environment-based configuration for provider credentials, concurrency limits, retry policy defaults, retention settings, and allowed egress endpoints. - CI/CD - GitHub Actions pipelines for CI and CD; required checks: tests, lint, types, security scan, build. - Backups/DR - PostgreSQL backups with RPO 15 minutes and RTO 60 minutes (per tech constraints). - Monitoring - Metrics: call attempt rate, completion/refusal/not-reachable rates, webhook error rate, provider API error rate, LLM latency, end-to-end conversational latency, queue lag, email send success. - Alerts: missing outcomes, webhook signature failures, queue backlog, elevated provider failures, latency SLO breaches. ## Risks & Mitigations - Regulatory non-compliance risk (telemarketing rules, consent wording) - Mitigation: require configurable scripts provided/approved by customer legal; enforce opt-out/do-not-call; maintain audit trails and retention controls. - Provider latency/quality affects completion rate and ≤1.5s target - Mitigation: instrument latency per turn; set concurrency and fallback responses; allow swapping provider adapter in future slices. - Duplicate/late webhooks causing inconsistent states - Mitigation: idempotency keys (provider_call_id + event_type); state machine constraints; transactional updates; dead-letter handling for SQS. - PII exposure via logs/exports - Mitigation: structured logging with redaction; role-gated export; audit every export; least-privilege access. - Operator error in CSV uploads leading to bad calling - Mitigation: strong validation, preview, and explicit “start campaign” confirmation with counts and excluded contacts summary. ## Assumptions - AWS is the deployment environment and EKS is used for workloads (from tech constraints; still marked assumption in YAML). - PostgreSQL, Redis, SQS, and an OIDC-compatible IdP are available and approved for use (from IDEA/constraints). - Slice-1 integrates exactly one telephony/voice AI provider; specific vendor (e.g., Twilio) is selected during implementation. - Email sending uses an existing enterprise-approved email service; adapter interface exists but provider specifics are configured per deployment. - English and Italian are supported end-to-end for Slice-1; additional languages are not required. - “local_telemarketing_rules” requirements are supplied by customer/legal; system provides mechanisms (opt-out, do-not-call, audit) but not legal templates. ## Success Metrics - TTFA: ≤15 minutes from first login to launching a simple campaign with a small test list (from IDEA). - Operator task success: ≥85% can upload contacts, configure campaign, and start without assistance (from IDEA). - Conversational latency: ≤1.5s P95 for ≥95% of turns (from IDEA). - Data integrity: ≤2% calls with missing/inconsistent outcome or survey data per campaign (from IDEA). - Dashboard freshness: metrics reflect events within 60 seconds (from IDEA). ## Acceptance Criteria - Given a CSV with 10 valid contacts and 2 invalid rows, when uploaded, then the system persists all 10 valid contacts, rejects exactly 2 rows, and returns per-row error reasons; overall upload processing completes within 60 seconds. - Given a campaign configured with intro + consent script + 3 questions + max_attempts=5 + a time window, when saved, then retrieving GET /campaigns/{id} returns the same values and the campaign appears in the campaign list within 5 seconds. - Given a running campaign with one reachable contact, when the system initiates a call, then the callee receives the identity/purpose/duration statement before any survey question and the system stores a Call record with a correlation_id and provider_call_id. - Given the callee explicitly refuses consent, when refusal is detected, then the call ends within 10 seconds, ContactState becomes refused, and a survey.refused event is emitted to SQS with campaign_id, contact_id, call_id, and timestamp. - Given the callee grants consent and answers all 3 questions, when the call completes, then a SurveyResponse exists with consent_granted=true and 3 captured answers, ContactState becomes completed, and a survey.completed event is emitted to SQS; the dashboard completed count increases within 60 seconds. - Given a contact has outcomes no_answer or busy, when a call attempt ends, then attempt_count increments by 1, next_attempt_at is scheduled within the configured time window, and no more than 5 total attempts occur for that contact. - Given 50+ call attempts in a campaign, when the user opens the dashboard, then it shows completed/refused/not-reachable counts and percentages consistent with stored ContactState within ±1 record and data freshness ≤60 seconds. - Given a user with role viewer requests an export, then the system denies access (HTTP 403) and writes an AuditEvent of type export.denied with correlation_id; given a user with role manager requests an export, then the system returns a CSV containing at least contact_id, phone, outcome, attempt_count, and (if completed) the 3 answers. ## Out Of Scope - Inbound or callback handling, call transfers, or human handoff. - Dynamic branching surveys, more than 3 questions, sentiment analysis, or advanced persuasion optimization. - Multi-tenant isolation features (tenant admin, tenant billing, tenant-level routing). - Multi-channel outreach beyond follow-up emails (no SMS/WhatsApp/web in Slice-1). - Advanced BI dashboards, forecasting, or CRM/ERP synchronization. ## Note from Harper Orchestrator (Super User) to be applied -
